chunks: Abi and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on them) said: It was narrated to us by Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, who raised it to one of the two Imams, al-Baqir or al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man has a daughter, Allah sends an angel to her, who brushes his wing over her head and chest and says: 'She is weak, created from weakness. One who spends on her will be helped on the Day of Judgment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for raising a daughter in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* underscores the spiritual merit of nurturing daughters by linking their physical fragility to divine mercy, noting that an angel blesses the newborn. It establishes a profound theological principle: the financial and emotional support provided to a daughter is recorded as a continuous act of worship (*mu'an*) that secures divine assistance until the Day of Judgment. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *sadaqah* and care within the family structure as a means of attaining nearness to God.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 4. Abi and Muhammad b. al-Hassan (rah) they said it was narrated to us by Ahmad b. Idris and Muhammad b. Yahya al-’Attarall of themfrom Muhammad b. Ahmad from Ya’qub b. Yazid who raised it to one of the two Imams al-Baqir or al-Sadiq (a.s.) who said:

“Whenever a girl is born, Allah appoints an angel near that child, who touches his wings over her head and chest saying: It is created with weakness. One who bears her expenses will be helped on the Day of Judgment.”
